$comment: Measured against Microsoft PowerPoint by experiment T5. Do not hand-edit: regenerate with tools/ground-truth/text/bullets/analyse.ts. See docs/adr/phase-3-text/0031-bullets-fields-and-script-runs.md.
method: Slide.Export(path, "EMF") records PowerPoint own GDI calls, so a bullet comes back as the characters it drew with the face, size and colour it drew them in. Paragraphs(i).BoundLeft gives the position in points, which the EMF cannot, and TextRange.Text gives a field value for the locales PowerPoint shapes into glyph ids before drawing.

B. what a scheme renders.name: measured
B. what a scheme renders.note: the tables, wrap points and biases read off the sweep

B. what a scheme renders.name: no-wrap
B. what a scheme renders.note: alphabetic counts grow without bound, so startAt=900 gives 35 letters

B. what a scheme renders.note: every alphabet wraps at 780, Hebrew included

B. what a scheme renders.note: no alphabet has the off-by-one, so Thai bands begin at 41k+1 like the rest

B. what a scheme renders.name: bijective
B. what a scheme renders.note: alphabetic numbering is bijective base-26, so 27 is "aa" and 53 is "ba"

B. what a scheme renders.name: hebrew-repeats
B. what a scheme renders.note: Hebrew repeats its current letter like Latin, so 26 is dalet-dalet

B. what a scheme renders.name: ascii-stop
B. what a scheme renders.note: the double-byte schemes take an ASCII full stop rather than U+FF0E

B. what a scheme renders.name: additive-roman
B. what a scheme renders.note: roman numerals are additive, so 4 is "iiii" and 9 is "viiii"

B. what a scheme renders.name: cjk-ideographic-zero
B. what a scheme renders.note: the East Asian zero is U+3007, the character a table of Chinese numerals gives

B. what a scheme renders.name: cjk-one-ten-rule
B. what a scheme renders.note: all three East Asian families share one ten-form rule

B. what a scheme renders.name: wingdings-no-wrap
B. what a scheme renders.note: the Wingdings circled numbers fall back to digits past ten instead of wrapping

B. what a scheme renders.name: circled-past-twenty
B. what a scheme renders.note: circled digits continue past 20 rather than falling back to ASCII

C. the numbering pass.name: measured
C. the numbering pass.note: same level, same scheme and same startAt; deeper levels skipped, shallower breaks

C. the numbering pass.name: one-counter
C. the numbering pass.note: one counter per text body, incremented by every numbered paragraph

C. the numbering pass.name: per-level-never-restart
C. the numbering pass.note: a counter per level that never restarts, so a nested list resumes where it left off

C. the numbering pass.name: startat-does-not-break
C. the numbering pass.note: the run is broken by a change of scheme but not by a change of startAt

C. the numbering pass.name: deeper-levels-break
C. the numbering pass.note: any intervening paragraph breaks the run, deeper ones included

C. the numbering pass.name: unnumbered-consumes
C. the numbering pass.note: an unnumbered paragraph takes a number without showing one

D. the private-use mapping for buChar.name: measured
D. the private-use mapping for buChar.note: a symbol face maps the ANSI codepage byte into U+F000..U+F0FF; other faces do not

D. the private-use mapping for buChar.name: never
D. the private-use mapping for buChar.note: the character is drawn exactly as written

D. the private-use mapping for buChar.name: always
D. the private-use mapping for buChar.note: every face maps the low range, so a section sign in Arial becomes U+F0A7

D. the private-use mapping for buChar.name: latin-1-only
D. the private-use mapping for buChar.note: only U+0020..U+00FF is mapped, so U+2022 is drawn as itself

D. the private-use mapping for buChar.name: low-byte
D. the private-use mapping for buChar.note: the code point is masked to its low byte rather than mapped through the codepage

E. which face draws the bullet.name: measured
E. which face draws the bullet.note: buFont for a character bullet; the run face for an autonumber, always

E. which face draws the bullet.name: buFont-for-both
E. which face draws the bullet.note: buFont applies to an autonumber as well, which is what the schema implies

E. which face draws the bullet.name: run-face-always
E. which face draws the bullet.note: buFont is decorative and the run face draws everything

E. which face draws the bullet.name: no-theme-resolution
E. which face draws the bullet.note: a theme reference is used as a literal typeface name

F. what size the bullet is drawn at.name: measured
F. what size the bullet is drawn at.note: buSzPct is a percentage of the first run size; buSzPts is absolute; else the run size

F. what size the bullet is drawn at.name: pct-of-defrpr
F. what size the bullet is drawn at.note: buSzPct is a percentage of the paragraph defRPr size where one is stated

F. what size the bullet is drawn at.name: pts-are-scaled
F. what size the bullet is drawn at.note: buSzPts is a percentage too, so 600 means six per cent

F. what size the bullet is drawn at.name: largest-run
F. what size the bullet is drawn at.note: the bullet follows the largest run in the paragraph rather than the first

G. what colour the bullet is drawn in.name: measured
G. what colour the bullet is drawn in.note: buClr where stated, whatever the bullet kind; otherwise the run colour

G. what colour the bullet is drawn in.name: text-colour-always
G. what colour the bullet is drawn in.note: buClr is decorative and the bullet follows the text, as buFont does for an autonumber

G. what colour the bullet is drawn in.name: char-only
G. what colour the bullet is drawn in.note: buClr reaches a character bullet but not an autonumber, matching buFont

G. what colour the bullet is drawn in.name: default-black
G. what colour the bullet is drawn in.note: a bullet with no buClr is black rather than following the text

H. what box a picture bullet occupies.name: measured
H. what box a picture bullet occupies.note: height is 0.7 x the font size, width follows the aspect ratio

H. what box a picture bullet occupies.name: square
H. what box a picture bullet occupies.note: a picture bullet is letterboxed into a square box, so the aspect ratio is ignored

H. what box a picture bullet occupies.name: full-em
H. what box a picture bullet occupies.note: the height is the font size itself rather than seven tenths of it

H. what box a picture bullet occupies.name: fixed-height
H. what box a picture bullet occupies.note: the height is a constant 16.8pt whatever the font size

I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.name: measured
I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.note: max(marL, -indent, bulletLeft + bullet), where a positive indent moves nothing

I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.name: indent-moves-both-ways
I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.note: a positive indent pushes the bullet right, as a first-line indent would

I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.name: no-clamp
I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.note: the bullet may be drawn left of the frame, so a hanging indent can pull it negative

I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.name: always-marL
I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.note: the text always starts at marL and a wide bullet overlaps it

I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.name: bullet-abuts
I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.note: the text always starts at the end of the bullet

I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.name: no-hanging-floor
I. where the text starts on a bulleted f.note: without the -indent term, a hanging indent wider than the bullet is ignored

J. where a wrapped line starts.name: measured
J. where a wrapped line starts.note: marL exactly, with no bullet and no clamp

J. where a wrapped line starts.name: clamped
J. where a wrapped line starts.note: the clamp that moves the first line applies to every line

J. where a wrapped line starts.name: first-line-position
J. where a wrapped line starts.note: every line lines up under the first line rather than under marL

K. which script slot draws a character.name: measured
K. which script slot draws a character.note: private use to sym; Hebrew, Arabic, Thai and Devanagari to cs; CJK to ea; else latin

K. which script slot draws a character.name: no-sym
K. which script slot draws a character.note: a:sym is never used and the private-use area falls to a:latin

K. which script slot draws a character.name: non-ascii-is-cs
K. which script slot draws a character.note: anything above Latin-1 goes to a:cs, which is how the name reads

K. which script slot draws a character.name: punct-is-ea
K. which script slot draws a character.note: general punctuation and currency follow the East Asian slot

K2. which face draws a character whose s.name: measured
K2. which face draws a character whose s.note: an absent slot falls straight to a:latin

K2. which face draws a character whose s.name: ea-then-cs
K2. which face draws a character whose s.note: an absent slot tries the other non-latin slots before a:latin

K2. which face draws a character whose s.name: no-fallback
K2. which face draws a character whose s.note: a character whose slot is absent is not drawn at all

L. whether a field shows its cached text.name: measured
L. whether a field shows its cached text.note: a reserved type is recomputed on open and the cache is never shown

L. whether a field shows its cached text.name: cache-wins
L. whether a field shows its cached text.note: the cached a:t is what the reader displays

renderedNote: Every scheme reading, keyed scheme -> source -> startAt, where the source is the face the probe used: p for Arial, m for Courier New, c for the one-at-a-time count sweep. A run of four or more identical characters is written char*count - a mechanical, lossless encoding, not a model: no scheme emits an asterisk, which the analysis asserts. Without it the forty-eight-letter readings alone push this file past the corpus size cap.
glyphRunNote: PowerPoint shapes the Arabic alphabetic schemes before drawing them, so their EMF records hold glyph ids rather than characters. The ids are kept - the repeat structure is still readable in them - but they are not compared as strings, because they are not text.
truncatedNote: Readings where the decoration the scheme name promises never appeared, so PowerPoint stopped emitting the string part-way. Twelve of 6071, all hindiAlphaPeriod between 769 and 780 where the bullet is forty-eight Devanagari vowels. Excluded from the scoring and kept here.
